mcqs.question: Which of the following sketches correctly shows three lines where each pair meets at a different point, forming a small triangle?

options.A: All three lines intersect at a single common point.
options.B: Each pair of lines meets at a different point, creating a triangle.
options.C: Two lines are parallel and the third cuts them.
options.D: All three lines are parallel and never meet.

mcqs.answer: Each pair of lines meets at a different point, creating a triangle.
mcqs.explanation: The correct sketch is the one where no two lines are parallel and no three lines pass through the same point. In that arrangement each pair intersects once, giving three distinct intersection points that form a triangle. Option A shows concurrency, C shows a parallel pair, and D shows no intersections, all of which do not meet the requirement.

mcqs.question: Line L1 is given by y = x, line L2 by y = -x + 6, and line L3 by x = 4. What are the coordinates of the intersection point of line L1 and line L3?
mcqs.explanation: Substituting x = 4 into L1 (y = x) gives y = 4, so the intersection of L1 and L3 is (4,4). Option A is the intersection of L1 and L2, B is L2 and L3, and D does not belong to any of the given lines.

mcqs.question: When three lines intersect at three different points forming a small triangle, what is the sum of the interior angles of that triangle?
mcqs.explanation: Any triangle, regardless of how it is formed, has interior angles that add up to 180°. The other totals correspond to the sum of angles around a point (360°) or are unrelated.

mcqs.question: Which description correctly characterises an arrangement where no two lines are parallel and no three lines meet at a single point?

options.A: All three lines intersect at a single point.
options.B: Each pair of lines intersect at a different point, forming a triangle.
options.C: Two lines are parallel and the third cuts them.

mcqs.answer: Each pair of lines intersect at a different point, forming a triangle.
mcqs.explanation: When no lines are parallel and no three are concurrent, each pair meets once, giving three distinct intersection points that outline a triangle. Options A, C, and D each violate one of the stated conditions.

mcqs.question: Consider two configurations of three lines: Config A – all three lines pass through the same point; Config B – each pair of lines meets at a different point. Which statement correctly distinguishes them?

options.A: Both configurations have the same number of intersection points.
options.B: Config A has one intersection point while Config B has three.
options.C: Config A has three intersection points while Config B has one.
options.D: Neither configuration has any intersection points.

mcqs.answer: Config A has one intersection point while Config B has three.
mcqs.explanation: In Config A the three lines are concurrent, giving a single common intersection. In Config B each pair meets separately, producing three distinct intersection points. Hence option B is correct; the others misstate the counts.

mcqs.question: With the same lines as in job 66 (L1: y = x, L2: y = -x + 6, L3: x = 4), which of the following points is NOT an intersection point of any two of these lines?
mcqs.explanation: (3,3) is L1∩L2, (4,4) is L1∩L3, (4,2) is L2∩L3. The point (5,5) does not satisfy any of the three line equations, so it is not an intersection point. Hence D is correct.

mcqs.question: When two straight lines intersect, they form vertical angles. What is the relationship between the measures of vertical angles?
mcqs.explanation: Vertical angles are opposite each other when two lines cross, and by definition they have the same measure. Options B, C, and D describe other angle relationships that do not apply to vertical angles.

mcqs.question: Which description best matches three lines that are all parallel to each other?

options.A: They never meet, so there are no intersection points.
options.B: All three lines intersect at a single common point.
options.C: Each pair of lines meets at a different point, forming a triangle.
options.D: Two lines are parallel and the third cuts them.

mcqs.answer: They never meet, so there are no intersection points.
mcqs.explanation: Parallel lines never intersect, so three parallel lines produce zero intersection points. The other options describe concurrent, distinct‑intersection, or mixed configurations, which are not parallel.
